findingDispositions.reason: Distinct verified family: malformed npm root -g output is accepted as a valid filesystem root, directly weakening the Story doctor diagnostic; it is applicable and requires repair in the current Story.

F-009 is verified and distinct: the CHK-003 implementation collapses statSync EACCES and every other non-ENOENT failure into binTargetExists=false with verification=ok, losing the errno and prescribing a rebuild for an access or filesystem failure. packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts and the corresponding hermetic global-core-realpath test are explicitly in this Story scope, and the false absence result undermines the promised user-visible doctor diagnostic. It is therefore applicable and requires repair in the current Story.
startsWith(..) rejects valid in-dist names like ..cli.js, so it is applicable and requires current Story repair.

Independent frozen-candidate probe placed /bin/echo at PATH npm: successful stdout root -g was accepted without filesystem-path validation, and globalCoreRealpath returned status=pass, installed=false, npmRoot=root -g. This directly confirms the structured npm-root probe can turn corrupt or wrapped output into a false known-absence result.

Independent hermetic probe created an existing executable bin beneath a mode-000 dist directory. The target stat failed with EACCES, yet the report recorded binMode=null, executable=false, verification=ok and warned that the target does not exist with rebuild remediation; source inspection confirms the catch has no errno discrimination. This is a distinct probe-error classification family.

Independent hermetic promoteDist helper probe used the valid package-relative target dist/..cli.js. path.relative returned the in-tree filename ..cli.js, but the startsWith(..) guard skipped it: restored=[] and mode remained 0644. This independently confirms a distinct lexical-prefix containment error in the promotion path.

Source inspection confirms restoreBinExecutableBits has separate string-shorthand and object-value iteration paths, while the registered red test's package fixtures declare only one-entry object-form bin values. Repository search found no string-form or multi-target assertion, so this is an independently supported coverage family distinct from F-010's containment predicate.

The committed diff removes the PIN MAINTENANCE block, while repository-wide search leaves exactly the live phrases 'the maintenance note above' and 'see PIN MAINTENANCE above' in validation-tier-planner-smoke.ts. The dangling maintenance guidance is independently confirmed and is a distinct residual-reference family.

restoreBinExecutableBits calls statSync(target).mode and chmodSync without checking isFile(). An independent temporary-package probe declared dist/cli.js as a directory and observed restored=['dist/cli.js'], isFile=false, isDirectory=true, mode=755. This verifies a non-regular-target acceptance family separate from path containment and shape coverage.

The smoke's harness ceiling and bounded wait call child.kill('SIGKILL') only on the direct CLI child, then resolve or await close; no process-group or descendant cleanup handle exists. The configured descendant command starts sleep 600, so failure paths can outlive the direct child. This is a distinct cleanup/lifecycle family.

descendantTreeCommand unconditionally executes /bin/sh with an external sleep 600 command, and proof-or-stop.config.json registers validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke without a platform guard. The same validation planner explicitly models win32 behavior, where /bin/sh is not a portable executable. This independently supports a platform-portability family distinct from descendant cleanup.

Confirmed independently on the current committed helper: package.json declared dist/cli.js, the path was an in-tree symlink to an outside 0644 file, restoreBinExecutableBits(dist) returned [dist/cli.js] and chmod followed the symlink, changing the outside referent to 0755. Source inspection shows lexical relative-path containment followed by statSync/chmodSync, with no lstat or resolved-target containment check. This is one verified symlink-escape family and is distinct from F-010 lexical traversal-prefix handling and F-013 non-regular target handling.

Independently verified that Story plan, checklist context, understanding, and summary still describe post-promotion chmod, while the committed implementation restores the staging tree before evicting the previous dist. This is a distinct Story-model consistency family, separate from intermediate-symlink containment and its missing regression coverage.

The registered red test unconditionally asserts POSIX 0o111 semantics even on Windows, where npm package execution uses command shims and chmod does not represent the same contract. This is a verified platform-portability family distinct from stale lifecycle wording.

The machine-owned CHK-001 must intent and ProofStory bind universal POSIX 0o111/0755 semantics while the repaired test defines a distinct Windows npm-shim target branch. The Windows branch can pass without emitting the pinned POSIX label, so the acceptance contract is internally inconsistent and requires repair.

F-025 isolates the exact pinned-selector failure already included in F-024: both cite checklist line 30 versus the Windows alternate label at red-global-cli-exec-bit lines 179-182 and require the same platform-invariant or platform-aware intent repair. F-024 is live, verified, and non-circular, so F-025 adds no independent family.

The CHK-003 shared fixture unconditionally constructs a directory symlink and expects POSIX 0644/X_OK/chmod behavior, while production explicitly treats win32 as having no execute-bit contract. This makes the registered ok-global-core-realpath evidence path fail or abort on affected Windows hosts and is distinct from CHK-001 acceptance wording.

CHK-003 happy evidence pins a submitter-specific absolute macOS checkout path, so the command cannot refresh in another clone or Windows checkout even if the correct doctor row is emitted. This path-binding defect is independent of the global-core test fixture portability and CHK-001 labels.

Verified as a distinct production-output family. runtime-environment-checks.ts uses POSIX-only shell quoting and emits cd -- / ls -ld remediation text on Windows, so the promised exact doctor remediation is not executable there. F-024/F-025 concern CHK-001 acceptance selectors, F-026 concerns Windows test-fixture portability, and F-027 concerns a host-bound evidence selector; none owns the emitted remediation-command defect.

Verified as a distinct production false-pass family: runtime-environment-checks.ts:693-695 returns executable=true solely from platform=win32, while :737-769 only stats the declared Node target and never validates the actual .cmd/.ps1 shim. The win32 fixture at global-core-realpath.test.mjs:1229-1240 creates no shim and merely asserts that unconditional verdict. This differs from F-026 fixture portability, F-027 selector portability, and F-028 remediation rendering.

Verified as the canonical recurrence of F-028: commandPathQuote at runtime-environment-checks.ts:703-717 preserves legal percent-delimited Windows path components even though cmd.exe expands %NAME% inside quoted command lines, and the test helper mirrors the same quoting with only a space-path fixture. The production surface and required fix are exactly the existing Windows doctor remediation-command portability family.

Verified as recurrence of F-024: checklist.json:10 and delivery-check.json:11-14 still bind the universal POSIX-only ls -la/-rwxr-xr-x user outcome, while checklist.json:25 and ProofStory AC-001 now define POSIX bits versus the Windows Node-target/npm-shim contract. The residual is within the existing cross-platform acceptance-contract family.

F-032 cites the same live source defect at commandPathQuote, the same legal %VAR%-shaped Windows path, the same cmd.exe expansion behavior, the same missing percent-path fixture, and the same remediation as earlier live F-030. F-030 is verified, open, current-wave, and the chain is non-circular.

Verified as a distinct evidence-integrity family: global-core-realpath.test.mjs:83-87 emits the exact accepted `ok global-core-realpath` selector and exits 0 before cases 1-34 when the Windows directory-link capability probe returns EPERM/EACCES/ENOSYS. This is not F-026's former Windows test failure/unreachability; the repair created the opposite failure mode, a mechanically accepted zero-assertion green, requiring skip isolation or a non-accepting selector.

Independent source inspection and a built-candidate temporary-filesystem probe confirmed that inspectGlobalCoreExecutable stat-follows the package.json bin target without checking its realpath containment: a canonical global package whose dist/cli.js symlinks into .worktrees/stale still reports global-core-realpath PASS and emits the pass marker. This is distinct from F-029's Windows npm command-shim selection and from F-016/F-017's already-repaired promotion-time symlink protections.

Independent source inspection and a built-candidate probe with commandResolver=null confirmed that cli-entrypoint reports missing while a healthy package under npm root makes global-core-realpath PASS with no remediation. CHK-003 promises informational link guidance when no global proof-or-stop is on PATH, but the global-core check classifies npm package presence instead. This is distinct from the Windows shim, quoting, platform-wording, and zero-assertion skip families.

Independent current-source inspection and a fresh temporary-filesystem probe confirmed that package.json EACCES is swallowed: the old 0755 dist is replaced by the new 0644 CLI without an exception. This is distinct from runtime or doctor probe-failure families and symlink-containment families because it occurs at promotion manifest discovery and converts an unverifiable input into successful mutation.

Current source still short-circuits the win32 executable probe to true at runtime-environment-checks.ts:693-695 and the Windows fixture at global-core-realpath.test.mjs:1236-1240 constructs no .cmd/.ps1 shim. This remains the distinct Windows command-shim validation family.

Current commandPathQuote at runtime-environment-checks.ts:703-707 wraps Windows paths in double quotes without preserving literal paired-percent components from cmd.exe expansion. This is the canonical Windows remediation-command portability family.

Checklist CHK-001.userSees still unconditionally promises POSIX ls/-rwxr-xr-x while its intent and ProofStory distinguish POSIX executable bits from Windows shim semantics. This remains the cross-platform acceptance-contract family.

F-032 cites the same live commandPathQuote implementation, the same cmd.exe percent expansion on legal Windows paths, the same missing percent-path fixture, and the same required literal-path remediation as signature-valid open F-030. F-030 is canonical and the duplicate chain is direct and non-circular.

global-core-realpath.test.mjs:83-87 still prints the accepted ok selector and exits 0 before all cases when the Windows directory-link capability probe is unavailable. This remains the distinct zero-assertion skip/false-green family.

inspectGlobalCoreExecutable still resolves the lexical package bin path then stat/access-follows it without verifying the target realpath remains inside the canonical package. This remains the distinct doctor bin-target realpath-escape family.

checkGlobalCoreRealpath still derives presence from npm root and package entry without consulting context.cliEntrypoint, while CHK-003 promises behavior for no global proof-or-stop on PATH. This remains the distinct PATH-versus-package-presence contract family.

restoreBinExecutableBits at promote-dist.mjs:87-91 still catches every package.json read/parse error and returns [], allowing non-absence read failures to proceed to old-dist eviction. This remains the distinct promotion manifest-read-error false-success family.
